items.title: Every closed subscheme of a relative Proj over a quasi-compact base is itself a relative Proj of a graded quotient
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact relative Proj, every closed subscheme is the relative Proj of the graded quotient by the kernel of the canonical map to the graded pushforward of its structure sheaf's twists (statement lines 7903-7917). The counted proof is a genuine local computation: it first obtains the closed immersion from the candidate quotient algebra and reduces to identifying two closed subschemes, then works on affine charts of a Proj, where the two inclusions between the defining ideals are proved by adjusting homogeneous elements with powers of the chart equation (using invertibility of the twists) and by comparing localizations of the local ideals across the charts (proof lines 7919-7983). It is H2: the reduction and both inclusions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard relative Proj and twist statements.
